-/
import Mathlib.FieldTheory.AlgebraicClosure
import Mathlib.FieldTheory.IntermediateField.Adjoin.Basic
import Mathlib.NumberTheory.Height.NumberField
import Mathlib.NumberTheory.NumberField.Discriminant.Different
import Mathlib.NumberTheory.NumberField.Completion.FinitePlace
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Radical.NatInt

set_option autoImplicit false

open NumberField IsDedekindDomain IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum
open scoped IntermediateField Classical

namespace AbcAdaptation.Tripod

abbrev Qbar : Type := AlgebraicClosure ℚ

/-- Algebraic points on the tripod, with zero and one removed. -/
def Pt : Type := {z : Qbar // z ≠ 0 ∧ z ≠ 1}

theorem isIntegral (z : Qbar) : IsIntegral ℚ z :=
  (AlgebraicClosure.isAlgebraic ℚ |>.isAlgebraic z).isIntegral

/-- Point degree as the degree of the minimal polynomial. -/
noncomputable def deg (z : Qbar) : ℕ := (minpoly ℚ z).natDegree

theorem deg_pos (z : Qbar) : 0 < deg z := minpoly.natDegree_pos (isIntegral z)

theorem deg_pos_real (z : Qbar) : (0 : ℝ) < deg z := by
  exact_mod_cast deg_pos z

noncomputable abbrev fieldOf (z : Qbar) : IntermediateField ℚ Qbar := ℚ⟮z⟯

instance (z : Qbar) : FiniteDimensional ℚ (fieldOf z) :=
  IntermediateField.adjoin.finiteDimensional (isIntegral z)

instance (F : IntermediateField ℚ Qbar) [FiniteDimensional ℚ F] : NumberField F where

theorem deg_eq_finrank (z : Qbar) : deg z = Module.finrank ℚ (fieldOf z) :=
  (IntermediateField.adjoin.finrank (isIntegral z)).symm

/-- The generator of the simple intermediate field `ℚ(z)`, identified with `z`. -/
noncomputable def gen (z : Qbar) : fieldOf z := IntermediateField.AdjoinSimple.gen ℚ z

@[simp] theorem coe_gen (z : Qbar) : (gen z : Qbar) = z :=
  IntermediateField.AdjoinSimple.coe_gen ℚ z

theorem gen_ne_zero {z : Qbar} (hz : z ≠ 0) : gen z ≠ 0 := by
  intro h
  apply hz
  simpa using congrArg (fun y : fieldOf z => (y : Qbar)) h

theorem gen_sub_one_ne_zero {z : Qbar} (hz : z ≠ 1) : gen z - 1 ≠ 0 := by
  intro h
  apply hz
  have h1 : gen z = 1 := sub_eq_zero.mp h
  have := congrArg (fun y : fieldOf z => (y : Qbar)) h1
  simpa using this

def ptLE (d : ℕ) : Set Pt := {x | deg x.1 ≤ d}

def ptEQ (d : ℕ) : Set Pt := {x | deg x.1 = d}

theorem mem_ptLE {d : ℕ} {x : Pt} : x ∈ ptLE d ↔ deg x.1 ≤ d := Iff.rfl

theorem mem_ptEQ {d : ℕ} {x : Pt} : x ∈ ptEQ d ↔ deg x.1 = d := Iff.rfl

theorem ptLE_zero : ptLE 0 = ∅ := by
  ext x
  simp only [mem_ptLE, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
  exact Nat.not_le.mpr (deg_pos x.1)

theorem ptLE_succ (d : ℕ) : ptLE (d + 1) = ptLE d ∪ ptEQ (d + 1) := by
  ext x
  simp only [mem_ptLE, Set.mem_union, mem_ptEQ]
  exact (Nat.le_succ_iff_eq_or_le).trans or_comm

/-- Mathlib's relative number-field logarithmic height, normalized by point degree. -/
noncomputable def htCan (x : Pt) : ℝ :=
  Height.logHeight₁ (gen x.1) / deg x.1

theorem htCan_nonneg (x : Pt) : 0 ≤ htCan x :=
  div_nonneg (Height.zero_le_logHeight₁ _) (Nat.cast_nonneg _)

theorem deg_mul_htCan (x : Pt) :
    (deg x.1 : ℝ) * htCan x = Height.logHeight₁ (gen x.1) := by
  rw [htCan, mul_div_cancel₀ _ (show (deg x.1 : ℝ) ≠ 0 by
    exact_mod_cast (deg_pos x.1).ne')]

/-- Log absolute discriminant, normalized by `[ℚ(z) : ℚ]`. -/
noncomputable def logDiff (x : Pt) : ℝ :=
  Real.log |(discr (fieldOf x.1) : ℝ)| / deg x.1

theorem one_le_abs_discr_real (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K] :
    (1 : ℝ) ≤ |(discr K : ℝ)| := by
  rw [← Int.cast_abs]
  exact_mod_cast Int.one_le_abs (discr_ne_zero K)

theorem logDiff_nonneg (x : Pt) : 0 ≤ logDiff x :=
  div_nonneg (Real.log_nonneg (one_le_abs_discr_real _)) (Nat.cast_nonneg _)

theorem logDiff_eq_log_absNorm_differentIdeal (x : Pt) :
    logDiff x =
      Real.log (Ideal.absNorm (differentIdeal ℤ (𝓞 (fieldOf x.1)))) / deg x.1 := by
  unfold logDiff
  rw [absNorm_differentIdeal (K := fieldOf x.1), Nat.cast_natAbs, Int.cast_abs]

def badPlaces (z : Qbar) : Set (FinitePlace (fieldOf z)) :=
  {v | v (gen z) ≠ 1 ∨ v (gen z - 1) ≠ 1}

theorem mem_badPlaces {z : Qbar} {v : FinitePlace (fieldOf z)} :
    v ∈ badPlaces z ↔ v (gen z) ≠ 1 ∨ v (gen z - 1) ≠ 1 := Iff.rfl

theorem badPlaces_finite {z : Qbar} (hz : z ≠ 0 ∧ z ≠ 1) :
    (badPlaces z).Finite := by
  have h₁ := FinitePlace.hasFiniteMulSupport (gen_ne_zero hz.1)
  have h₂ := FinitePlace.hasFiniteMulSupport (gen_sub_one_ne_zero hz.2)
  refine (h₁.union h₂).subset fun v hv => ?_
  rcases hv with hv | hv
  · exact Or.inl hv
  · exact Or.inr hv

/-- Sum of residue-norm logarithms over finite places meeting `{0,1,∞}`. -/
noncomputable def logCond (x : Pt) : ℝ :=
  (∑ᶠ v : FinitePlace (fieldOf x.1),
    if v ∈ badPlaces x.1 then Real.log (Ideal.absNorm v.maximalIdeal.asIdeal) else 0) /
    deg x.1

theorem one_le_absNorm_real {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]
    (v : FinitePlace K) : (1 : ℝ) ≤ Ideal.absNorm v.maximalIdeal.asIdeal := by
  exact_mod_cast (NumberField.HeightOneSpectrum.one_lt_absNorm v.maximalIdeal).le

theorem logCond_nonneg (x : Pt) : 0 ≤ logCond x := by
  classical
  apply div_nonneg _ (Nat.cast_nonneg _)
  apply finsum_nonneg
  intro v
  split_ifs
  · exact Real.log_nonneg (one_le_absNorm_real v)
  · exact le_rfl

theorem logCond_eq_sum (x : Pt) :
    logCond x = (∑ v ∈ (badPlaces_finite x.2).toFinset,
      Real.log (Ideal.absNorm v.maximalIdeal.asIdeal)) / deg x.1 := by
  classical
  unfold logCond
  congr 1
  rw [finsum_eq_sum_of_support_subset (s := (badPlaces_finite x.2).toFinset)]
  · rw [Finset.sum_ite_of_true]
    intro v hv
    simpa using hv
  · intro v hv
    simp only [Function.mem_support, ne_eq, ite_eq_right_iff, Classical.not_imp] at hv
    simpa using hv.1

/-- The residue characteristic of the actual quotient of the ring of integers. -/
noncomputable def residueChar {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]
    (v : FinitePlace K) : ℕ :=
  ringChar (𝓞 K ⧸ v.maximalIdeal.asIdeal)

/-- A finite prime support containing `2` and a real valuation bound. -/
structure CompactlyBounded where
  V : Finset ℕ
  prime : ∀ p ∈ V, p.Prime
  two_mem : 2 ∈ V
  c : ℝ

def CompactlyBounded.set (K : CompactlyBounded) : Set Pt :=
  {x | (∀ v : FinitePlace (fieldOf x.1), residueChar v ∈ K.V →
      |Real.log (v (gen x.1))| ≤ K.c ∧ |Real.log (v (gen x.1 - 1))| ≤ K.c) ∧
    ∀ w : InfinitePlace (fieldOf x.1),
      |Real.log (w (gen x.1))| ≤ K.c ∧ |Real.log (w (gen x.1 - 1))| ≤ K.c}

theorem CompactlyBounded.mem_set {K : CompactlyBounded} {x : Pt} :
    x ∈ K.set ↔
      (∀ v : FinitePlace (fieldOf x.1), residueChar v ∈ K.V →
        |Real.log (v (gen x.1))| ≤ K.c ∧ |Real.log (v (gen x.1 - 1))| ≤ K.c) ∧
      ∀ w : InfinitePlace (fieldOf x.1),
        |Real.log (w (gen x.1))| ≤ K.c ∧ |Real.log (w (gen x.1 - 1))| ≤ K.c := Iff.rfl

/-- The rational point `q` in the algebraic closure, with zero and one excluded. -/
noncomputable def rationalPoint (q : ℚ) (h0 : q ≠ 0) (h1 : q ≠ 1) : Pt :=
  ⟨algebraMap ℚ Qbar q,
    fun h => h0 ((algebraMap ℚ Qbar).injective (h.trans (map_zero _).symm)),
    fun h => h1 ((algebraMap ℚ Qbar).injective (h.trans (map_one _).symm))⟩

/-- Statement I, fully unfolded: no compactly bounded restriction. -/
def StatementI : Prop :=
  ∀ (d : ℕ) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x : Pt, deg x.1 ≤ d →
    htCan x ≤ (1 + ε) * (logDiff x + logCond x) + C

/-- Statement II, fully unfolded: the same inequality on each bounded set. -/
def StatementII : Prop :=
  ∀ (d : ℕ) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∀ K : CompactlyBounded, ∃ C : ℝ,
    ∀ x : Pt, x ∈ K.set → deg x.1 ≤ d →
      htCan x ≤ (1 + ε) * (logDiff x + logCond x) + C

def DegreeOneProjection : Prop :=
  ∀ (q : ℚ) (h0 : q ≠ 0) (h1 : q ≠ 1), deg (rationalPoint q h0 h1).1 = 1

def LogDifferentZeroProjection : Prop :=
  ∀ (q : ℚ) (h0 : q ≠ 0) (h1 : q ≠ 1), logDiff (rationalPoint q h0 h1) = 0

def HeightComparisonProjection : Prop :=
  ∀ (q : ℚ) (h0 : q ≠ 0) (h1 : q ≠ 1),
    Height.logHeight₁ q ≤ htCan (rationalPoint q h0 h1)

def RadicalConductorProjection : Prop :=
  ∀ (q : ℚ) (h0 : q ≠ 0) (h1 : q ≠ 1),
    logCond (rationalPoint q h0 h1) ≤
      Real.log
        ((UniqueFactorizationMonoid.radical
          (q.num * (q.num - (q.den : ℤ)) * (q.den : ℤ)) : ℤ) : ℝ)

end AbcAdaptation.Tripod
natural_language_statement:
> “Thus, it follows from the equivalence of [GenEll], Theorem 2.1, that, in order to complete the proof of Corollary 2.3, it suffices to verify that [GenEll], Theorem 2.1, (ii), holds.”

— Shinichi Mochizuki, *Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV*, §2, proof of Corollary 2.3.

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Qbar`

Defines $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ to be the algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Pt`

Defines the type of points to consist of elements $z$ of the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$, together with proofs that $z\ne0$ and $z\ne1$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.isIntegral`

For every $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}$, where $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ is the algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q$, the element $z$ is integral over $\mathbb Q$: it satisfies a monic polynomial with rational coefficients. There is no exclusion of $0$ or $1$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.deg`

For every $z$ in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$, defines its degree to be the natural-number degree of its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb Q$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.deg_pos`

For every $z$ in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$, the natural-number degree of the minimal polynomial of $z$ over $\mathbb Q$ is strictly positive, including when $z=0$ or $z=1$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.deg_pos_real`

For every $z$ in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$, the degree of its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb Q$, cast from $\mathbb N$ to $\mathbb R$, is strictly greater than $0$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.fieldOf`

For every $z$ in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$, defines the intermediate field $\mathbb Q(z)\subseteq\overline{\mathbb Q}$ to be the smallest intermediate field containing $z$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.anonymous_instance_finiteDimensional_fieldOf`

For every $z$ in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$, supplies the assertion that the simple intermediate field $\mathbb Q(z)\subseteq\overline{\mathbb Q}$ is finite-dimensional as a vector space over $\mathbb Q$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.anonymous_instance_numberField_intermediateField`

For every intermediate field $F$ between $\mathbb Q$ and its algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, assuming $F$ is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb Q$, supplies a number-field structure on $F$; its field operations and characteristic-zero structure are those inherited from this intermediate field.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.deg_eq_finrank`

For every $z$ in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$, the natural-number degree of its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb Q$ equals the dimension $[\mathbb Q(z):\mathbb Q]$ of the smallest intermediate field containing $z$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.gen`

For every $z$ in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$, defines an element of the simple intermediate field $\mathbb Q(z)$: its distinguished generator, whose image under the inclusion into $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ is $z$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.coe_gen`

For every $z$ in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$, the distinguished generator of the simple intermediate field $\mathbb Q(z)$, viewed as an element of $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ through the inclusion, equals $z$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.gen_ne_zero`

For every $z$ in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$, if $z\ne0$, then the element of $\mathbb Q(z)$ whose image under inclusion is $z$ is nonzero in $\mathbb Q(z)$. No assumption $z\ne1$ is imposed.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.gen_sub_one_ne_zero`

For every $z$ in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$, if $z\ne1$, then $g-1\ne0$ in $\mathbb Q(z)$, where $g\in\mathbb Q(z)$ is the element whose image under inclusion is $z$. No assumption $z\ne0$ is imposed.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.ptLE`

For every natural number $d$, including $d=0$, defines the set of points $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}$ with $z\ne0$, $z\ne1$, and minimal-polynomial degree over $\mathbb Q$ at most $d$; each point includes proofs of the two exclusions.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.ptEQ`

For every natural number $d$, including $d=0$, defines the set of points $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}$ with $z\ne0$, $z\ne1$, and minimal-polynomial degree over $\mathbb Q$ exactly $d$; each point includes proofs of the two exclusions.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.mem_ptLE`

For every natural number $d$ and every point represented by $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}$ with proofs of $z\ne0$ and $z\ne1$, membership in the set of such points of degree at most $d$ is equivalent to the inequality $\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))\le d$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.mem_ptEQ`

For every natural number $d$ and every point represented by $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}$ with proofs of $z\ne0$ and $z\ne1$, membership in the set of such points of degree exactly $d$ is equivalent to $\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))=d$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.ptLE_zero`

The set of points represented by $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}$ with $z\ne0$, $z\ne1$, and minimal-polynomial degree over $\mathbb Q$ at most $0$ is the empty set.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.ptLE_succ`

For every natural number $d$, the set of points $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$ whose minimal-polynomial degree over $\mathbb Q$ is at most $d+1$ equals the union of the set of such points of degree at most $d$ and the set of such points of degree exactly $d+1$. This includes $d=0$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.htCan`

For every point represented by $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$, put $F=\mathbb Q(z)$, let $g\in F$ be the element mapping to $z$, and let $n$ be the degree of the minimal polynomial of $z$ over $\mathbb Q$. Defines its real height to be $\operatorname{logHeight}_{1,F}(g)/n$, where the numerator is Mathlib's relative number-field logarithmic height computed in $F$ and the natural number $n$ is cast to $\mathbb R$. The normalization is division by the point degree, which equals $[F:\mathbb Q]$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.htCan_nonneg`

For every $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$, let $F=\mathbb Q(z)$, let $g\in F$ map to $z$, and let $n=\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))$. Then $0\le\operatorname{logHeight}_{1,F}(g)/n$, where the numerator is Mathlib's relative number-field logarithmic height and $n$ is cast to $\mathbb R$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.deg_mul_htCan`

For every $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$, with $F=\mathbb Q(z)$, $g\in F$ mapping to $z$, and $n=\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))$, the real equality $n\bigl(\operatorname{logHeight}_{1,F}(g)/n\bigr)=\operatorname{logHeight}_{1,F}(g)$ holds. Here $\operatorname{logHeight}_{1,F}$ is Mathlib's relative number-field logarithmic height, and both occurrences of $n$ are real casts.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.logDiff`

For every point represented by $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$, defines the real quantity $\log|\operatorname{discr}(\mathbb Q(z))|/n$, where $\operatorname{discr}(\mathbb Q(z))\in\mathbb Z$ is the number-field discriminant, cast to $\mathbb R$ before taking absolute value and natural logarithm, and $n=\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))=[\mathbb Q(z):\mathbb Q]$ is cast to $\mathbb R$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.one_le_abs_discr_real`

For every type $K$ equipped with a field structure and a number-field structure, the integer discriminant of $K$, cast to $\mathbb R$, satisfies $1\le|\operatorname{discr}(K)|$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.logDiff_nonneg`

For every $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$, one has $0\le\log|\operatorname{discr}(\mathbb Q(z))|/\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))$. The integer discriminant and natural-number degree are cast to $\mathbb R$, and $\log$ is the natural logarithm.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.logDiff_eq_log_absNorm_differentIdeal`

For every $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$, put $F=\mathbb Q(z)$ and $n=\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))$. Then $\log|\operatorname{discr}(F)|/n=\log N(\mathfrak D_{\mathcal O_F/\mathbb Z})/n$, where $\mathcal O_F$ is the ring of integers of $F$, $\mathfrak D_{\mathcal O_F/\mathbb Z}$ is its different ideal over $\mathbb Z$, and $N$ is the ideal's absolute norm, the cardinality of the quotient by that ideal. All quantities entering the real logarithms and divisions are cast to $\mathbb R$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.badPlaces`

For every $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}$, including $0$ and $1$, put $F=\mathbb Q(z)$ and let $g\in F$ map to $z$. Defines a set of finite places of $F$ by $B_z=\{v:v(g)\ne1\ \lor\ v(g-1)\ne1\}$, using the multiplicative absolute values supplied by the finite places. When $z=0$ or $z=1$, this set contains every finite place.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.mem_badPlaces`

For every $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}$ and every finite place $v$ of $F=\mathbb Q(z)$, let $g\in F$ map to $z$. Membership of $v$ in the set $\{u:u(g)\ne1\lor u(g-1)\ne1\}$ is equivalent to $v(g)\ne1\lor v(g-1)\ne1$. There is no assumption excluding $z=0$ or $z=1$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.badPlaces_finite`

For every $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}$, assuming both $z\ne0$ and $z\ne1$, the set of finite places $v$ of $F=\mathbb Q(z)$ satisfying $v(g)\ne1$ or $v(g-1)\ne1$ is finite, where $g\in F$ is the element mapping to $z$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.logCond`

For every point represented by $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$, put $F=\mathbb Q(z)$, let $g\in F$ map to $z$, and let $n=\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))$. Defines the real quantity $\frac1n\sum_{v\in B_z}\log\#(\mathcal O_F/\mathfrak p_v)$, where $B_z=\{v\text{ a finite place of }F:v(g)\ne1\lor v(g-1)\ne1\}$ and $\mathfrak p_v$ is the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_F$ associated to $v$. Literally the numerator is a finite-support sum over all finite places, with summand $\log N(\mathfrak p_v)$ on $B_z$ and $0$ elsewhere; $B_z$ is finite, so this is the ordinary finite sum displayed. Each place occurs once, with no additional weight besides its log absolute ideal norm, and the sum is divided by the real cast of $n=[F:\mathbb Q]$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.one_le_absNorm_real`

For every type $K$ equipped with a field structure and a number-field structure, and every finite place $v$ of $K$, the absolute norm of its associated maximal ideal $\mathfrak p_v\subseteq\mathcal O_K$, cast to $\mathbb R$, satisfies $1\le N(\mathfrak p_v)=\#(\mathcal O_K/\mathfrak p_v)$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.logCond_nonneg`

For every $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$, put $F=\mathbb Q(z)$, let $g\in F$ map to $z$, and let $n=\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))$. Then $0\le\frac1n\sum_{v\in B_z}\log\#(\mathcal O_F/\mathfrak p_v)$, where $B_z$ is the finite set of all finite places $v$ of $F$ with $v(g)\ne1$ or $v(g-1)\ne1$, and $\mathfrak p_v$ is the corresponding maximal ideal of the ring of integers. This sum has one term per such place, no further weights, and real casts of its norms and denominator.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.logCond_eq_sum`

For every $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$, put $F=\mathbb Q(z)$, let $g\in F$ map to $z$, let $n=\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))$, and let $B_z=\{v\text{ a finite place of }F:v(g)\ne1\lor v(g-1)\ne1\}$. The finite-support sum over all finite places of the function that is $\log\#(\mathcal O_F/\mathfrak p_v)$ on $B_z$ and zero elsewhere, divided by the real cast of $n$, equals $\frac1n\sum_{v\in B_z}\log\#(\mathcal O_F/\mathfrak p_v)$. On the right, the sum is over the finite set obtained from the proved finiteness of exactly $B_z$, with each place counted once and no additional weight.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.residueChar`

For every type $K$ equipped with a field structure and a number-field structure, and every finite place $v$ of $K$, defines a natural number equal to the ring characteristic of the actual quotient ring $\mathcal O_K/\mathfrak p_v$, where $\mathcal O_K$ is the ring of integers and $\mathfrak p_v$ is the maximal ideal associated to $v$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.CompactlyBounded`

Defines a structure consisting of a finite set $V\subseteq\mathbb N$, a proof that every $p\in V$ is prime, a proof that $2\in V$, and a real number $c$. No nonnegativity or positivity condition is imposed on $c$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.CompactlyBounded.set`

For every structure $K$ consisting of a finite set $V\subseteq\mathbb N$ of primes containing $2$ and an unrestricted real number $c$, defines a set of points $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$ as follows. Put $F=\mathbb Q(z)$ and let $g\in F$ map to $z$. Membership requires both: for every finite place $v$ of $F$, if $\operatorname{char}(\mathcal O_F/\mathfrak p_v)\in V$, then $|\log v(g)|\le c$ and $|\log v(g-1)|\le c$; and for every infinite place $w$ of $F$, $|\log w(g)|\le c$ and $|\log w(g-1)|\le c$. No bound is required at finite places whose residue characteristic is outside $V$. If $c<0$, the defined set is empty.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.CompactlyBounded.mem_set`

For every structure $K$ consisting of a finite set $V\subseteq\mathbb N$ of primes containing $2$ and a real number $c$, and every point represented by $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$, put $F=\mathbb Q(z)$ and let $g\in F$ map to $z$. Membership in the set assigned to $K$ is equivalent to the conjunction of: for every finite place $v$ of $F$, $\operatorname{char}(\mathcal O_F/\mathfrak p_v)\in V$ implies $|\log v(g)|\le c\land|\log v(g-1)|\le c$; and for every infinite place $w$ of $F$, $|\log w(g)|\le c\land|\log w(g-1)|\le c$. The real number $c$ need not be nonnegative, and the finite-place condition imposes nothing outside the specified residue characteristics.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.rationalPoint`

For every rational number $q$, every proof $h_0$ that $q\ne0$, and every proof $h_1$ that $q\ne1$, defines a point whose underlying element is the image of $q$ under the canonical field embedding $\mathbb Q\to\overline{\mathbb Q}$, together with proofs that this image is neither $0$ nor $1$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.StatementI`

Defines the following proposition. For a point $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$, put $F_z=\mathbb Q(z)$, let $g_z\in F_z$ map to $z$, let $n_z=\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))=[F_z:\mathbb Q]$, and put $B_z=\{v\text{ a finite place of }F_z:v(g_z)\ne1\lor v(g_z-1)\ne1\}$. For every $d\in\mathbb N$ and every $\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$ with $0<\varepsilon$, there exists $C\in\mathbb R$ such that every such point with $n_z\le d$ satisfies $\frac{\operatorname{logHeight}_{1,F_z}(g_z)}{n_z}\le(1+\varepsilon)\left(\frac{\log|\operatorname{discr}(F_z)|}{n_z}+\frac{\sum_{v\in B_z}\log\#(\mathcal O_{F_z}/\mathfrak p_v)}{n_z}\right)+C$. The height in the numerator is Mathlib's relative number-field logarithmic height; each denominator is the real cast of the point degree. The sum is over exactly the finite set $B_z$, once per place, without additional weights. The constant may depend on $d$ and $\varepsilon$ but is uniform in the point, has no required sign, and there is no bounded-set restriction. The quantifier over $d$ includes $0$, for which the point condition is empty.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.StatementII`

Defines the following proposition. For each $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$, put $F_z=\mathbb Q(z)$, let $g_z\in F_z$ map to $z$, let $n_z=\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))$, and let $B_z=\{v\text{ a finite place of }F_z:v(g_z)\ne1\lor v(g_z-1)\ne1\}$. For every $d\in\mathbb N$ and every real $\varepsilon>0$, for every finite set $V\subseteq\mathbb N$ whose members are prime and which contains $2$, and every real $c$, there exists $C\in\mathbb R$ such that every such point satisfies the following implication: if $|\log v(g_z)|\le c$ and $|\log v(g_z-1)|\le c$ for every finite place $v$ with $\operatorname{char}(\mathcal O_{F_z}/\mathfrak p_v)\in V$, if $|\log w(g_z)|\le c$ and $|\log w(g_z-1)|\le c$ for every infinite place $w$, and if $n_z\le d$, then $\frac{\operatorname{logHeight}_{1,F_z}(g_z)}{n_z}\le(1+\varepsilon)\left(\frac{\log|\operatorname{discr}(F_z)|}{n_z}+\frac{\sum_{v\in B_z}\log\#(\mathcal O_{F_z}/\mathfrak p_v)}{n_z}\right)+C$. The height is Mathlib's relative logarithmic height divided by the real point degree; the conductor sum is over exactly the finite set $B_z$, once per place without extra weights, and is divided by that same degree. The constant may depend on $d,\varepsilon,V,c$ but not on the point, and has no sign condition. Finite places outside the specified residue characteristics are unrestricted. Both $d=0$ and arbitrary negative $c$ are included; in either case the eligible point set is empty.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.DegreeOneProjection`

Defines the proposition that for every $q\in\mathbb Q$, every proof $h_0:q\ne0$, and every proof $h_1:q\ne1$, the image $z$ of $q$ under the canonical embedding into the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ has minimal-polynomial degree over $\mathbb Q$ exactly $1$.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.LogDifferentZeroProjection`

Defines the proposition that for every $q\in\mathbb Q$ and every pair of proofs $q\ne0$ and $q\ne1$, if $z$ is its image in the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, $F=\mathbb Q(z)$, and $n=\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))$, then $\log|\operatorname{discr}(F)|/n=0$. The integer discriminant is cast to $\mathbb R$ before taking its absolute value and natural logarithm, and the natural-number point degree is cast to $\mathbb R$ for division.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.HeightComparisonProjection`

Defines the proposition that for every $q\in\mathbb Q$ and every pair of proofs $q\ne0$ and $q\ne1$, writing $q=a/b$ in reduced form with $a\in\mathbb Z$ and $b\in\mathbb N$ positive, letting $z$ be its image in $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, $F=\mathbb Q(z)$, $g\in F$ the element mapping to $z$, and $n=\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))$, one has $\log\max(|a|,b)=\operatorname{logHeight}_{1,\mathbb Q}(q)\le\operatorname{logHeight}_{1,F}(g)/n$. The right-hand numerator is Mathlib's relative number-field logarithmic height computed in $F$, divided by the real cast of the point degree.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.RadicalConductorProjection`

Defines the proposition that for every $q\in\mathbb Q$ and every pair of proofs $q\ne0$ and $q\ne1$, writing its reduced numerator and positive denominator as $a\in\mathbb Z$ and $b\in\mathbb N$, and putting $z$ equal to its image in $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, $F=\mathbb Q(z)$, $g\in F$ equal to the element mapping to $z$, $n=\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))$, and $B_z=\{v\text{ a finite place of }F:v(g)\ne1\lor v(g-1)\ne1\}$, one has $\frac1n\sum_{v\in B_z}\log\#(\mathcal O_F/\mathfrak p_v)\le\log\bigl(\operatorname{rad}_{\mathbb Z}(a(a-b)b)\bigr)$. The sum is over exactly the finite set $B_z$, once per place with no additional weights, and is divided by the real cast of the point degree. The product inside the radical is formed in $\mathbb Z$, including the cast of $b$ to $\mathbb Z$; the radical is the integer radical, namely the positive product of the distinct prime divisors of $|a(a-b)b|$, and its integer value is cast to $\mathbb R$ before taking the natural logarithm. The hypotheses ensure this product is nonzero.

各有理数 $q$、$q\ne0$ の各証明 $h_0$、および $q\ne1$ の各証明 $h_1$ に対し、標準的な体の埋め込み $\mathbb Q\to\overline{\mathbb Q}$ による $q$ の像を元とし、その像が $0$ でも $1$ でもないことの証明を伴う点を定義する。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.StatementI`

次の命題を定義する。点 $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$ に対し、$F_z=\mathbb Q(z)$ とし、$g_z\in F_z$ を $z$ に移る元、$n_z=\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))=[F_z:\mathbb Q]$、$B_z=\{v\text{ は }F_z\text{ の有限素点}:v(g_z)\ne1\lor v(g_z-1)\ne1\}$ とする。すべての $d\in\mathbb N$ と $0<\varepsilon$ を満たす実数 $\varepsilon$ に対し、実数 $C$ が存在し、$n_z\le d$ を満たすすべての点で $\frac{\operatorname{logHeight}_{1,F_z}(g_z)}{n_z}\le(1+\varepsilon)\left(\frac{\log|\operatorname{discr}(F_z)|}{n_z}+\frac{\sum_{v\in B_z}\log\#(\mathcal O_{F_z}/\mathfrak p_v)}{n_z}\right)+C$ が成り立つ。高さの分子は $F_z$ で計算する Mathlib の相対的な数体の対数的高さであり、各分母は点の次数を実数に移した値である。和はちょうど有限集合 $B_z$ 上で取り、各素点を一度だけ数え、追加の重みは付けない。定数は $d$ と $\varepsilon$ に依存してよいが点には一様であり、符号の条件はなく、有界集合への制限もない。$d=0$ も量化の対象であり、この場合は点の条件を満たすものがない。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.StatementII`

次の命題を定義する。各 $z\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$ に対し、$F_z=\mathbb Q(z)$ とし、$g_z\in F_z$ を $z$ に移る元、$n_z=\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))$、$B_z=\{v\text{ は }F_z\text{ の有限素点}:v(g_z)\ne1\lor v(g_z-1)\ne1\}$ とする。すべての $d\in\mathbb N$ と実数 $\varepsilon>0$ に対し、さらに、すべての元が素数で $2$ を含む任意の有限集合 $V\subseteq\mathbb N$ と任意の実数 $c$ に対し、実数 $C$ が存在し、各点について次の含意が成り立つ。$\operatorname{char}(\mathcal O_{F_z}/\mathfrak p_v)\in V$ を満たすすべての有限素点 $v$ で $|\log v(g_z)|\le c$ かつ $|\log v(g_z-1)|\le c$、すべての無限素点 $w$ で $|\log w(g_z)|\le c$ かつ $|\log w(g_z-1)|\le c$、さらに $n_z\le d$ ならば、$\frac{\operatorname{logHeight}_{1,F_z}(g_z)}{n_z}\le(1+\varepsilon)\left(\frac{\log|\operatorname{discr}(F_z)|}{n_z}+\frac{\sum_{v\in B_z}\log\#(\mathcal O_{F_z}/\mathfrak p_v)}{n_z}\right)+C$ である。高さは Mathlib の相対的な対数的高さを実数に移した点の次数で割ったものである。導手の和はちょうど有限集合 $B_z$ 上で各素点を一度だけ数え、追加の重みを付けず、同じ次数で割る。定数は $d,\varepsilon,V,c$ に依存してよいが点には依存せず、符号の条件もない。指定された剰余標数以外の有限素点には制約を課さない。$d=0$ と任意の負の $c$ も含み、いずれの場合も条件を満たす点の集合は空である。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.DegreeOneProjection`

すべての $q\in\mathbb Q$、すべての証明 $h_0:q\ne0$、およびすべての証明 $h_1:q\ne1$ について、代数閉包 $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ への標準的な埋め込みによる $q$ の像 $z$ の、$\mathbb Q$ 上の最小多項式の次数がちょうど $1$ であるという命題を定義する。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.LogDifferentZeroProjection`

各 $q\in\mathbb Q$ と、$q\ne0$ および $q\ne1$ の各証明の組について、$z$ を代数閉包 $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ における像、$F=\mathbb Q(z)$、$n=\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))$ とすると、$\log|\operatorname{discr}(F)|/n=0$ となるという命題を定義する。整数判別式を実数に移してから絶対値と自然対数を取り、自然数値の点の次数も実数に移して除算に用いる。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.HeightComparisonProjection`

各 $q\in\mathbb Q$ と、$q\ne0$ および $q\ne1$ の各証明の組について、$q=a/b$ を $a\in\mathbb Z$、正の $b\in\mathbb N$ による既約分数表示とする。$z$ を $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ における像、$F=\mathbb Q(z)$、$g\in F$ を $z$ に移る元、$n=\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))$ とすると、$\log\max(|a|,b)=\operatorname{logHeight}_{1,\mathbb Q}(q)\le\operatorname{logHeight}_{1,F}(g)/n$ が成り立つという命題を定義する。右辺の分子は $F$ で計算する Mathlib の相対的な数体の対数的高さであり、実数に移した点の次数で割る。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.RadicalConductorProjection`

各 $q\in\mathbb Q$ と、$q\ne0$ および $q\ne1$ の各証明の組について、既約表示の分子を $a\in\mathbb Z$、正の分母を $b\in\mathbb N$ とする。$z$ を $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ における像、$F=\mathbb Q(z)$、$g\in F$ を $z$ に移る元、$n=\deg(\operatorname{minpoly}_{\mathbb Q}(z))$、$B_z=\{v\text{ は }F\text{ の有限素点}:v(g)\ne1\lor v(g-1)\ne1\}$ とすると、$\frac1n\sum_{v\in B_z}\log\#(\mathcal O_F/\mathfrak p_v)\le\log\bigl(\operatorname{rad}_{\mathbb Z}(a(a-b)b)\bigr)$ が成り立つという命題を定義する。和はちょうど有限集合 $B_z$ 上で各素点を一度だけ数え、追加の重みを付けず、実数に移した点の次数で割る。根基の中の積は $b$ も整数に移して $\mathbb Z$ で計算する。根基は整数上の根基、すなわち $|a(a-b)b|$ の相異なる素因数すべての正の積であり、その整数値を実数に移して自然対数を取る。仮定によりこの積は非零である。
